articles.title: Anodized Rainbow
articles.summary: Smooth low-roughness surface with soft warped rainbow interference bands, like oil on metal. A soft rippled, liquid sheen with no distinct shapes; reads like a smooth oxidised metal with a watery shimmer.
articles.what: Anodized titanium / niobium oxide rainbow bands — smooth low-roughness surface with FBM-warped interference banding from oxide thickness gradient, R=Metallic Up close: Warped, wavy interference ripples like water or thumbprint contour lines, 10-25 px wide, flowing in irregular waves with no cells or edges. Inside the highlight they show as lighter and darker wobbling bands; outside they melt to a faint wobble. From a distance: A soft rippled, liquid sheen with no distinct shapes; reads like a smooth oxidised metal with a watery shimmer. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Optical & Interference (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Optical & Interference", or search for "Anodized Rainbow".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and fenders: broad flats show the flow
Pair with a colour-shifting base paint if you want actual rainbow hue
Numbers keep colour and shape; ripples are soft and do not cut edges.
Mild: soft wobbling bands inside the highlight, a subtle watery satin
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a rainbow paint: despite the name this spec adds no hue, colour only comes from paint or other layers
Not holographic flake: no sparkle points
Avoid: matte base, dark colors.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
